hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 今天; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: Today and this year are useful anchors for a first classroom diary. 今 connects these time phrases without requiring a new character for every date.

components.explanation: The 人-shaped roof covers a short dot and a hooked lower stroke. There is no extra dot beneath that hook.

readingNotes: 今 is jīn with a first tone in 今天 and 今年. Do not confuse its level tone with the fourth tone of 进 (jìn).
usage: 今 usually needs a following time word: 今天 means today and 今年 means this year. It is not normally used alone as a complete answer to 'when'.
writingTip: Spread the two roof strokes enough to shelter the centre, then leave clear space between the inner dot and the lower hook.

exampleSentences.meaning: I am at home today.
I am studying Chinese this year.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 今天我们先写字，再读书。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒmen xiān xiě zì, zài dú shū.
exampleSentences.meaning: Today we will write characters first, then read.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 令 has an additional lower dot; adding that mark to 今 creates a different character.

seo.title: 今 (jīn) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 今 (jīn): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 今 (jīn) for today and this year. Compare its lower hook with 令, watch the stroke sequence, and practise useful time expressions.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 明天; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: Learners use 明天 to arrange the next lesson and 明白 to check understanding. The visible 日 and 月 also make 明 a useful two-component writing exercise.

components.explanation: 日 stands on the left and 月 on the right. Keep the enclosed 日 compact beside the taller, narrower 月.

readingNotes: 明 is míng with a rising second tone. 明白 is commonly míngbai, with a neutral final syllable; the reading of 明 stays unchanged.
usage: 明天 means tomorrow, while 明年 means next year. In 明白, the same character contributes to understanding or clarity rather than naming a future date.
writingTip: Keep the two boxes of 日 even; start 月 high enough that its upper edge aligns with the top of the left component.

exampleSentences.meaning: See you tomorrow!

exampleSentences.pinyin: Nǐ míngbai wǒ de yìsi ma?
exampleSentences.meaning: Do you understand what I mean?

exampleSentences.hanzi: 明年我想和朋友去中国。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Míngnián wǒ xiǎng hé péngyou qù Zhōngguó.
exampleSentences.meaning: Next year I would like to go to China with friends.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 朋 repeats 月 on both sides, whereas 明 starts with 日. Check the left component before adding the inner horizontals.

seo.title: 明 (míng) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 明 (míng): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 明 (míng) with 日 and 月, tomorrow and next-year examples, and a comparison with 朋. Follow the animation to balance both sides.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 昨天; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: A short account of yesterday introduces past events without changing a verb ending. 昨 helps learners recognise 昨天 and compare it with 今天 and 明天.

components.explanation: A narrow 日 sits beside 乍. On the right, a short upper slant leads into a vertical crossed by short horizontal strokes.

readingNotes: 昨 is zuó with a second tone. Keep the initial z distinct from the zh in 桌 (zhuō); yesterday is zuótiān.
usage: 昨 occurs most often in 昨天, yesterday. 昨晚 and 昨夜 both refer to last night; 昨日 is a more written alternative to 昨天.
writingTip: Give 日 less than half the width, and keep the short bars of 乍 separated so the right side does not become a dark block.

exampleSentences.meaning: It was cold yesterday.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Wǒ zuówǎn dú le zhè běn shū.
exampleSentences.meaning: I read this book last night.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 昨天老师教我们写了三个新字。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Zuótiān lǎoshī jiāo wǒmen xiě le sān gè xīn zì.
exampleSentences.meaning: Yesterday the teacher taught us to write three new characters.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 作 uses 亻 on the left, while 昨 uses 日. The shared 乍 does not make these words interchangeable.

seo.title: 昨 (zuó) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 昨 (zuó): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Practise 昨 (zuó) in yesterday and last-night expressions. See how its 日 side differs from 作 and follow the complete writing sequence.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 时候; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: Asking when a lesson starts and saying how long it lasts need different time expressions. 时 connects 时候, 时间, and 小时 while keeping those uses distinct.

components.explanation: The simplified form places 日 on the left and 寸 on the right. The small dot belongs inside the open space beside the right vertical hook.

readingNotes: 时 is shí, a second-tone retroflex syllable. In 时候 (shíhou), 候 is usually neutral, but 时 keeps its rising tone.
usage: 时间 names time in general, 小时 is an hour of duration, and 时候 is used when asking or describing when something happens. Use 点, rather than 时 alone, for ordinary spoken clock times.
writingTip: Write a slim 日 first, then leave enough space around the dot in 寸 that it does not touch the hook or horizontal.

exampleSentences.meaning: I have time.
When will you go home?

exampleSentences.hanzi: 我每天用一个小时读书和写字。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān yòng yí gè xiǎoshí dú shū hé xiě zì.
exampleSentences.meaning: I spend an hour reading and writing every day.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 日 is only the left component of 时. Omitting 寸 changes the word from time to day or sun.

seo.title: 时 (shí) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 时 (shí): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 时 (shí), the simplified counterpart of 時. Distinguish 时间, 小时, and 时候, with stroke animation and practical time sentences.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 分钟; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: Reading a clock and understanding a test score both require 分. Its alternative reading also makes it a useful early example of choosing pronunciation by word.

components.explanation: 八 opens out above 刀. The lower knife-shaped component contains a turning hook and a left-falling stroke.

readingNotes: Use fēn for 分钟, dividing, and scores. The same character is fèn in 部分 (bùfen, often neutral in speech) and 分外 (fènwài); choose the reading from the word.
usage: 分 measures minutes after an hour, as in 三点十分, and also appears in scores such as 九十分. 分开 means to separate; these uses share fēn but do not share one English translation.
writingTip: Keep the two upper strokes apart, leave a gap above 刀, and avoid extending the lower slant into the upper left stroke.

exampleSentences.meaning: Please wait five minutes.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Xiànzài shì sān diǎn shí fēn.
exampleSentences.meaning: It is ten past three now.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 老师把这些书分给了学生。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Lǎoshī bǎ zhèxiē shū fēn gěi le xuésheng.
exampleSentences.meaning: The teacher distributed these books to the students.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 八 is the upper part of 分; the lower 刀 is essential for 分 and must not be dropped.

seo.title: 分 (fēn) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 分 (fēn): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 分 (fēn) for minutes, scores, and dividing. Compare its 八-over-刀 form and understand when the alternative reading fèn applies.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 点; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: 点 connects telling the time with small quantities and restaurant orders. These everyday meanings give learners several reasons to recognise the same written form.

components.explanation: 占 occupies the top, with a small 口 beneath its upright stroke. Four separate dots form 灬 along the bottom.

readingNotes: 点 is diǎn with a third tone. In 一点儿, 儿 adds an r ending in accents that use erhua; it is not a separate full syllable.
usage: 点 names clock hours in 三点 and a small amount in 一点儿. 点菜 means to order food, while a written dot is also a 点; learn the whole phrase to identify the sense.
writingTip: Centre the upper 占 above all four bottom dots and keep those dots separate, spreading the outer pair slightly outward.

exampleSentences.meaning: What time is it now?
I can speak a little Chinese.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 我们六点到饭店以后再点菜。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Wǒmen liù diǎn dào fàndiàn yǐhòu zài diǎn cài.
exampleSentences.meaning: We will order after we reach the restaurant at six.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 占 lacks the four bottom dots of 点. Those marks are part of the character, not optional punctuation.

seo.title: 点 (diǎn) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 点 (diǎn): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: See 点 (diǎn) stroke order, its four bottom dots, and uses for clock time, small amounts, and ordering food. Compare simplified 点 with 點.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 前面; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: Directions and schedules both use 前. Comparing 前面 with 三天前 shows how position in a phrase distinguishes a place from an earlier time.

components.explanation: The top has two short strokes above a horizontal. Beneath it sit a 月-shaped section on the left and 刂 on the right.

readingNotes: 前 is qián with a rising tone. Its q initial is the same as in 钱 (qián), money, but the two characters have different meanings.
usage: 前面 describes the space in front, while 以前 means before a reference time. In 三天前, 前 follows the duration and means three days ago.
writingTip: Leave room under the top horizontal for both lower sections; keep the right vertical hook taller than the short vertical beside it.

exampleSentences.meaning: He is in front.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Qiántiān wǒ mǎi le yì běn shū.
exampleSentences.meaning: I bought a book the day before yesterday.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 上课以前，请把名字写在纸上。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Shàng kè yǐqián, qǐng bǎ míngzi xiě zài zhǐ shàng.
exampleSentences.meaning: Before class, please write your name on the paper.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 前 and 后 are opposite directions or times, but their shapes are unrelated. Learn 前面 and 后面 as a pair without copying one form into the other.

seo.title: 前 (qián) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 前 (qián): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 前 (qián) for in front, before, and ago. Follow its lower 月-shaped section and 刂, then practise spatial and time expressions.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 后面; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: 后 helps describe where someone stands and what happens next. Its meaning-dependent traditional forms are worth learning before relying on automatic conversion.

components.explanation: Two upper left-falling strokes frame a horizontal and a small 口 below. The simplified shape is open on its lower-right side.

readingNotes: 后 is hòu with a fourth tone. Traditional writing uses 後 for after or behind, but 后 remains 后 in 皇后, queen; conversion depends on meaning.
usage: 后面 means behind and 以后 means after or later. Place 后 after a duration for a later time, as in 三天后. 皇后 uses a separate queen sense and a different traditional-form rule.
writingTip: Keep the upper slants above and to the left of 口; the small box should sit beneath the horizontal rather than extend beyond it.

exampleSentences.meaning: He is behind me.
We will go to school the day after tomorrow.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 吃饭以后，我想和你一起看书。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Chī fàn yǐhòu, wǒ xiǎng hé nǐ yìqǐ kàn shū.
exampleSentences.meaning: After eating, I would like to read with you.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 右 begins with a horizontal crossed by a slant; 后 has an extra upper slant. Count the upper strokes before writing the box.

seo.title: 后 (hòu) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 后 (hòu): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 后 (hòu) for behind and after. See why traditional 後 applies to these senses but not 皇后, with animation and sentence examples.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 里; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: 里 lets a learner put familiar objects inside familiar places. It also appears in distance units, where the traditional spelling follows a different rule.

components.explanation: A 田-shaped upper section continues into 土 below. The central vertical runs through the upper box and joins the lower horizontals.

readingNotes: 里 is lǐ as an independent syllable; in 这里 (zhèli) and 那里 (nàli) it is often neutral. Inside is 裡 or 裏 in traditional writing; the distance unit stays 里.
usage: Use 里 after a place or container, as in 家里 and 书包里. 公里 means kilometre, a distance word rather than an inside location; its 里 does not become 裡.
writingTip: Keep the central vertical straight through the middle, and make the final horizontal broad enough to support the enclosed upper section.

exampleSentences.meaning: The book is in the bag.
There are many people here.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 从我家到学校有三公里。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Cóng wǒ jiā dào xuéxiào yǒu sān gōnglǐ.
exampleSentences.meaning: It is three kilometres from my home to school.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 田 has no extra horizontal base beneath the box; 里 extends the central vertical downward into a 土-shaped base.

seo.title: 里 (lǐ) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 里 (lǐ): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Practise 里 (lǐ) for inside and distance words. Compare 里 with 田 and learn when traditional writing uses 裡, 裏, or unchanged 里.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 2 vocabulary PDF includes 外; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: 外 makes useful pairs with 里 and connects location words to foreign-language study. Learners can reuse it in school, travel, and outdoor activities.

components.explanation: 夕 appears on the left and 卜 on the right. The right vertical is upright, with a short dot extending away from it.

readingNotes: 外 is wài with a falling fourth tone. Say the entire wai syllable together rather than separating it into two syllables.
usage: 外面 means outside, while 外国 means a foreign country and 外语 means a foreign language. The place after 外 is not always physical: 课外 refers to activities outside class.
writingTip: Leave a narrow channel between 夕 and the right vertical, then keep the final dot short so it does not compete with the left slant.

exampleSentences.meaning: It is cold outside.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xué yì mén wàiyǔ.
exampleSentences.meaning: I would like to learn a foreign language.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 下课以后，我们到外面走一走。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Xià kè yǐhòu, wǒmen dào wàimiàn zǒu yi zǒu.
exampleSentences.meaning: After class, we will go outside for a short walk.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 多 stacks two 夕 shapes; 外 has one 夕 beside 卜. The right side should not become another curved 夕.

seo.title: 外 (wài) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 外 (wài): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 外 (wài), its 夕 and 卜 shape, and words for outside, foreign countries, and languages. Follow the strokes and compare it with 多.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 2 vocabulary PDF includes 左边; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: Left-hand and left-turn instructions are easy to demonstrate in class. 左 is also a useful contrast with 右 because their inner components and opening strokes differ.

components.explanation: The upper horizontal and left-falling stroke shelter 工. Inside 工, a vertical connects two separate horizontal strokes.

readingNotes: 左 is zuǒ with a third tone. Its initial z is unaspirated; avoid changing it to the c of 错 (cuò).
usage: 左边 identifies the left side, and 向左 or 往左 tells someone to move left. 左右 can mean left and right, but after a quantity it can also mean approximately.
writingTip: Write the top horizontal before the slant, and leave enough space for 工 beneath it without closing its open sides.

exampleSentences.meaning: Please go left.
The book is on your left.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 我们下午三点左右到学校。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Wǒmen xiàwǔ sān diǎn zuǒyòu dào xuéxiào.
exampleSentences.meaning: We will reach school at about three in the afternoon.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 左 contains 工 and begins with a horizontal; 右 contains 口 and begins with a slant. Their similar outlines do not share every stroke step.

seo.title: 左 (zuǒ) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 左 (zuǒ): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 左 (zuǒ) and compare its 工 with 右's 口. Learn left-side directions and the approximate-quantity use of 左右 through examples.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 2 vocabulary PDF includes 右边; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue. This supports the word family, not a standalone character-level assignment.

importance: 右 helps learners follow directions and identify the right hand. It also exposes an English translation trap: the side meaning is separate from being correct.

components.explanation: A left-falling stroke crosses the upper horizontal, with 口 fitted beneath them. The box is closed, unlike the open 工 in 左.

readingNotes: 右 is yòu with a fourth tone. It sounds like 又, also yòu, but the two characters have different forms and uses.
usage: 右边 names the right side and 右手 means right hand. Use 向右 or 往右 for a direction; English 'right' meaning correct is usually 对, not 右.
writingTip: Begin with the slant before the upper horizontal, then keep 口 below the crossing point with a clear interior.

exampleSentences.meaning: Please go right.
My right hand is cold.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 到了学校门口以后向右转。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Dào le xuéxiào ménkǒu yǐhòu xiàng yòu zhuǎn.
exampleSentences.meaning: Turn right after reaching the school gate.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 右 encloses a small 口 rather than 工. Its opening slant also comes before the horizontal, unlike 左.

seo.title: 右 (yòu) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 右 (yòu): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Practise 右 (yòu), its slant-first opening, and its contrast with 左. Use right-hand and direction phrases without confusing right with correct.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 开; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: Opening a door, starting a lesson, and driving a car all use 开. A compact four-stroke character therefore supports several useful classroom and travel verbs.

components.explanation: Two horizontals sit above and across a lower left-falling stroke and a vertical. The simplified form has no surrounding 門 enclosure.

readingNotes: 开 is kāi with a level first tone. The same reading appears in 开门, 开始, and 开车 even though the verbs have different English meanings.
usage: 开门 means to open a door, 开始 means to begin, and 开车 means to drive. Pair 开 with 关 when describing opening and closing or switching something on and off.
writingTip: Keep the top horizontal shorter than the second; let both lower strokes extend below the long crossing horizontal.

exampleSentences.meaning: Please open the door.
We will start writing characters now.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 爸爸每天开车去学校接我。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Bàba měitiān kāi chē qù xuéxiào jiē wǒ.
exampleSentences.meaning: Dad drives to school to pick me up every day.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 井 has four crossing strokes arranged like a well frame; 开 starts with two horizontals and then a lower slant and vertical. Watch the animation rather than treating them as identical grids.

seo.title: 开 (kāi) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 开 (kāi): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 开 (kāi) for opening, starting, and driving. Follow its simplified four-stroke form and compare it with traditional 開 and similar 井.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 3 vocabulary PDF includes 关; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: 关 pairs naturally with 开 for door and light instructions. It also helps learners recognise the reassuring phrase 没关系 without translating every character literally.

components.explanation: Two short upper strokes sit above a 天-shaped lower section. The final left- and right-falling strokes spread beneath the horizontals.

readingNotes: 关 is guān with a level first tone. In 没关系 (méi guānxi), 系 is normally neutral; keep 关 clear and level.
usage: 关门 means to close a door and 关灯 means to turn off a light. 没关系 is a reassuring 'it does not matter'; its 关系 is a compound, not an instruction to close something.
writingTip: Keep the top pair small, separate the two horizontal levels, and balance the final spreading strokes around the centre.

exampleSentences.meaning: Please close the door.
It is all right; come again tomorrow.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Líkāi jiàoshì yǐqián, qǐng guān dēng.
exampleSentences.meaning: Please turn off the light before leaving the classroom.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 关 adds two short upper strokes above a 天-shaped body. Leaving them out changes the character to 天.

seo.title: 关 (guān) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 关 (guān): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 关 (guān) for closing and switching off. Compare it with 天, explore 没关系, and see the simplified form alongside traditional 關.

meaning: return; turn around; time or occasion

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 回; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: Returning home and answering a teacher are common beginner tasks. 回 supports both, while its nested boxes provide a clear enclosure-order writing exercise.

components.explanation: A small 口 sits inside a larger 囗 enclosure. Finish the inner box before closing the bottom of the outer frame.

readingNotes: 回 is huí with a second tone. In 回来 and 回去, the directional complement may be lighter in speech, while 回 keeps the main rising tone.
usage: 回家 means to go home, 回来 means to come back, and 回答 means to answer. The destination or following word tells you whether 回 describes returning or responding.
writingTip: Centre the small box with visible space on every side, and leave the outer bottom open until the inner strokes are complete.

exampleSentences.meaning: I have gone home.
When will you come back?

exampleSentences.hanzi: 请先看问题，然后回答老师。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Qǐng xiān kàn wèntí, ránhòu huídá lǎoshī.
exampleSentences.meaning: Please read the question first, then answer the teacher.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 口 contains one empty box; 回 has a second, smaller box inside. Do not merge the inner bottom with the outer enclosure.

seo.title: 回 (huí) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 回 (huí): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Follow 回 (huí) stroke order, including when to close the outer box. Practise returning home, coming back, and answering with clear examples.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 2 vocabulary PDF includes 出; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: Exits and outward movement use 出 in signs and conversation. Pairing it with 进 gives learners a practical way to distinguish opposite directions.

components.explanation: Two open-top 凵 shapes are joined by one central vertical. The lower section is wider, giving the stacked form a stable base.

readingNotes: 出 is chū with a first tone. Distinguish its aspirated ch from the unaspirated zh of 住 (zhù).
usage: 出去 means to go out, 出来 means to come out, and 出口 is an exit. The choice between 来 and 去 depends on movement toward or away from the reference point.
writingTip: Keep both open tops clear, carry the middle vertical through the form, and make the bottom section slightly wider than the top.

exampleSentences.meaning: Please come out.
The exit is on your right.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 下课以后，我们一起出去走走。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Xià kè yǐhòu, wǒmen yìqǐ chū qù zǒuzou.
exampleSentences.meaning: After class, let us go out for a walk together.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 山 has one lower open-top outline; 出 has two levels. Do not omit the upper side strokes when writing 出.

seo.title: 出 (chū) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 出 (chū): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 出 (chū), its two open-top levels, and the difference between 出来 and 出去. Watch the sequence and practise exit and movement words.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 2 vocabulary PDF includes 进; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: 进 is useful in both classroom invitations and descriptions of learning progress. Its 辶 component also prepares learners to compare movement-related character forms.

components.explanation: 井 sits above the sweeping 辶 component. The walking component is written after the inner 井 in this simplified form.

readingNotes: 进 is jìn with a fourth tone. It differs in tone and meaning from 今 (jīn), the first character of 今天.
usage: 进来 means to come in and 进去 means to go in. 进步 describes making progress, so the movement idea can also describe learning rather than walking into a room.
writingTip: Complete 井 first, then write 辶 with a long final sweep that supports the inner form without cutting through it.

exampleSentences.meaning: Please come in.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Nǐ de Hànyǔ jìnbù hěn kuài.
exampleSentences.meaning: Your Chinese is improving quickly.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 老师让我们先进去，再坐下。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Lǎoshī ràng wǒmen xiān jìn qù, zài zuò xià.
exampleSentences.meaning: The teacher asked us to go in first, then sit down.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 近 contains 斤 inside 辶; 进 contains 井. The shared walking component and similar sound do not make their meanings the same.

seo.title: 进 (jìn) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 进 (jìn): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 进 (jìn) with 井 inside 辶. Compare 进 and 近, practise entering and making progress, and view the traditional counterpart 進.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 2 vocabulary PDF includes 走; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: Walking to school and telling someone that you are leaving both use 走. Its contrast with 足 links an everyday action to a related body-part character.

components.explanation: 土 forms the upper section. Below it, a vertical and short horizontal lead into the left-falling stroke and long right-falling finish.

readingNotes: 走 is zǒu with a third tone. Keep its initial z distinct from the zh in 周 (zhōu).
usage: 走路 means to walk, while 我走了 can mean 'I am leaving'. 走开 tells someone to move away and can sound abrupt; 请往这边走 is a more polite direction.
writingTip: Keep the upper 土 compact and reserve space for the long final right-falling stroke, which carries the lower form outward.

exampleSentences.meaning: Let us go.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān zǒu lù qù xuéxiào.
exampleSentences.meaning: I walk to school every day.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Qǐng wǎng qián zǒu, zài xiàng zuǒ zhuǎn.
exampleSentences.meaning: Please walk forward, then turn left.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 足 starts with 口, while 走 starts with 土. Their lower shapes are similar, so check the top before writing.

seo.title: 走 (zǒu) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 走 (zǒu): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Practise 走 (zǒu) for walking and leaving. Compare its 土 top with 足, follow the sweeping final stroke, and learn polite directions.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 坐; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: 坐 is needed for classroom seating and travelling as a passenger. Comparing it with 座 prevents a common same-sound writing error.

components.explanation: Two small 人 shapes sit above a broad 土 base. The central vertical runs between them and continues into the lower section.

readingNotes: 坐 is zuò with a fourth tone. 座 has the same pronunciation, but is used for seats and as a classifier, not as the ordinary verb 'sit'.
usage: 坐下 means to sit down. 坐车 and 坐火车 describe travelling as a passenger; use 开车 when you mean driving the vehicle yourself.
writingTip: Keep the two 人 shapes small and separated by the centre line; use a broad final horizontal to support the whole character.

exampleSentences.meaning: Please sit down.
I travel to school by vehicle.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 我们坐火车去北京，不开车。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò huǒchē qù Běijīng, bù kāi chē.
exampleSentences.meaning: We are taking a train to Beijing, not driving.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 座 adds a 广 enclosure around 坐. Write 坐 for the action of sitting, and 座 in 座位, a seat.

seo.title: 坐 (zuò) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 坐 (zuò): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 坐 (zuò) for sitting and travelling by vehicle. See the two 人 shapes over 土, compare 坐 with 座, and practise passenger phrases.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 3 vocabulary PDF includes 站; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: 站 connects a classroom action, standing up, with a travel destination, a station. Its two-component form can be practised alongside 坐 as an action contrast.

components.explanation: 立 is compressed on the left, beside 占 on the right. The right side has a vertical above a small 口.

readingNotes: 站 is zhàn with a fourth tone and a retroflex zh. Avoid replacing it with the plain z in 暂 (zàn).
usage: 站 can be the verb stand, as in 站起来, or the noun station in 车站. 网站 extends the station idea to a website, so the meaning depends on the compound.
writingTip: Keep 立 narrow and let its final stroke rise slightly as a left-side component; place the right 口 below the upper horizontal.

exampleSentences.meaning: Please stand up.
The station is in front of the school.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 明天我们在火车站见面。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Míngtiān wǒmen zài huǒchēzhàn jiàn miàn.
exampleSentences.meaning: We will meet at the train station tomorrow.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 占 is only the right part of 站. The left 立 distinguishes standing or a station from the separate character 占.

seo.title: 站 (zhàn) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 站 (zhàn): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 站 (zhàn) with 立 and 占. Distinguish standing from a station, follow the animation, and practise train-station and everyday examples.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 买; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: Buying a book or a ticket is a concrete first shopping task. 买 is especially valuable when practised beside 卖 so that tone and shape reinforce the distinction.

components.explanation: A horizontal hook caps the simplified 头-shaped lower section. Two small dots sit above a horizontal crossed by the final long slant and dot.

readingNotes: 买 is mǎi with a third tone, while 卖 is mài with a fourth tone. The tone contrast changes buying into selling.
usage: 买 takes the thing purchased as its object: 买书 means to buy books. 买给 describes buying something for someone, while 买到 stresses successfully obtaining it.
writingTip: Keep the top hook distinct from the lower section, and place the two inner dots above the long horizontal rather than on it.

exampleSentences.meaning: I want to buy books.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Nǐ zài nǎr mǎi de piào?
exampleSentences.meaning: Where did you buy the ticket?

exampleSentences.hanzi: 我给妈妈买了一本汉语书。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Wǒ gěi māma mǎi le yì běn Hànyǔ shū.
exampleSentences.meaning: I bought a Chinese-language book for Mum.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 卖 has an extra 十 above the 买-shaped portion. Compare both the extra strokes and the third-tone versus fourth-tone pronunciation.

seo.title: 买 (mǎi) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 买 (mǎi): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 买 (mǎi), buying phrases, and its contrast with 卖 (mài). Follow the simplified shape and compare it with traditional 買.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 2 vocabulary PDF includes 卖; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: 卖 completes the buyer-and-seller contrast with 买. Sold-out signs and simple shop descriptions give the fourth-tone word an immediate practical setting.

components.explanation: 十 sits above the 买-shaped lower portion. Keep the top cross separate from the hooked horizontal beneath it.

readingNotes: 卖 is mài with a falling fourth tone. 买 is mǎi with a third tone; practise the pair aloud as well as comparing their shapes.
usage: 卖 describes selling an item, and 卖给 introduces its buyer. 卖完 means sold out; 卖掉 focuses on disposing of something by selling it.
writingTip: Keep 十 small so the lower strokes still have room; do not let the top vertical run into the hook below.

exampleSentences.meaning: Books are sold here.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Jīntiān de piào mài wán le.
exampleSentences.meaning: Today's tickets are sold out.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 他把不用的书卖给了朋友。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Tā bǎ bú yòng de shū mài gěi le péngyou.
exampleSentences.meaning: He sold the books he no longer used to a friend.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 买 lacks the upper 十 of 卖. Leaving it out reverses the transaction, and changing mài to mǎi also changes the spoken word.

seo.title: 卖 (mài) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 卖 (mài): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Practise 卖 (mài) for selling and sold-out items. Compare its extra 十 with 买, learn the tone contrast, and view traditional 賣.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 钱; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: 钱 is central to asking prices and handling small change. Its metal component links a common shopping word to the wider 金 character family.

components.explanation: The metal component 钅 is narrow on the left. 戋 occupies the right, with two horizontals crossed by a slanting hook and a final dot.

readingNotes: 钱 is qián with a rising second tone. It sounds the same as 前, but the metal component helps distinguish the written money word.
usage: 多少钱 asks a price, while 花钱 means to spend money and 省钱 means to save money by spending less. 钱 alone does not specify a currency.
writingTip: Reserve more width for 戋, keep its two horizontals separate, and place the final dot clearly above the right side of the slanting hook.

exampleSentences.meaning: How much is this book?
I do not have any small change.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Zǒu lù qù xuéxiào kěyǐ shěng qián.
exampleSentences.meaning: Walking to school can save money.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 线 has 纟 on the left instead of 钱's 钅. Both share 戋 on the right, so identify the left component before writing.

seo.title: 钱 (qián) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 钱 (qián): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Write 钱 (qián) with the metal component 钅. Learn price questions and spending phrases, compare 钱 with 线, and see traditional 錢.

hsk.note: The University of Manchester Confucius Institute's HSK 1 vocabulary PDF includes 本; this also matches the local HSK 2.0 catalogue.

importance: 本 lets learners count the books they use every day. Its short added line also offers a precise, easily checked contrast with 木.

components.explanation: 本 uses the 木 shape with an extra short horizontal near the foot of the central vertical. The added line is lower than 木's main crossbar.

readingNotes: 本 is běn with a third tone. In 本子 (běnzi), 子 is neutral; 本 keeps its lexical third tone, often shortened before another syllable.
usage: 本 counts books and similar bound volumes: 一本书. 本子 means a notebook, while 本来 means originally; the classifier meaning does not replace every use of 本.
writingTip: Write the 木-shaped strokes first, then add the short lower horizontal. Keep that line visibly shorter than the main upper crossbar.

exampleSentences.meaning: This is my notebook.

exampleSentences.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng běn shū.
exampleSentences.meaning: I bought two books.

exampleSentences.hanzi: 请把名字写在课本的第一页。
exampleSentences.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ míngzi xiě zài kèběn de dì yī yè.
exampleSentences.meaning: Please write your name on the first page of the textbook.

confusableCharacter.guidance: 木 lacks the short line near the bottom of 本. Do not move the added line to the top, which would suggest a different form.

seo.title: 本 (běn) Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.h1: How to Write 本 (běn): Stroke Order, Meaning & Examples
seo.description: Learn 本 (běn), the short line that distinguishes it from 木, and its use for counting books. Practise 一本书, 本子, and original-meaning examples.
